semantics: semantics.md (normative: deadlines, revisions, idempotency, commit-before-event, epochs, replay)
description: Closed command and event list of the v0.3 view-model service (docs/41 section 5). Request and result names refer to $defs in view-service.schema.json. 'adapters' lists where a command exists; elsewhere it returns capability_unavailable. 'wave' is the implementation wave in docs/43. 'effects' is 'none' for every command but one: catalogue rows, preferences, feedback, collections, grants and saved simulations are Loomward's own state, never a file or process effect. The exception is diagnostics.save, 'owner_picked_export': Loomward's own previewed bytes written to a file the owner picks in a native save dialog (docs/42 ADR-V3-24). Any new command needs a coordinator-reviewed contract PR; a contract test rejects names matching (delete|move|rename|kill|exec|shell|trim|suspend|priority|uninstall|write_file|run_command).

http.call: POST /api/v3/call  (Content-Type: application/json, X-Loomward-Token, body = RequestEnvelope, max 65536 bytes) -> 200 ResponseEnvelope
http.events: GET /api/v3/events  (Accept: text/event-stream, X-Loomward-Token, optional Last-Event-ID: '<epoch>.<seq>') -> SSE frames 'id: <epoch>.<seq>', 'event: <EventName>', 'data: <EventEnvelope JSON>'
http.assets: GET / and /assets/* serve app/dist when built; no token required for static assets

tauri.events: invoke('lw_events', { channel: Channel<EventEnvelope>, lastEpoch: string | null, lastSeq: number | null }) -> null; events arrive on the channel

roots.request_grant.note: Rust opens the native folder picker. HTTP: capability_unavailable; browser roots come only from loomward-serve --grant-root.

roots.forget.note: Owner decision q-9. Only for an already revoked root (an active one is refused with reason root_active). Purges Loomward's own display path, catalogue rows and the learning and collection rows that belong only to that root, and keeps an anonymised grants.list record (grant id, granted_at, revoked_at, forgotten_at). Never touches a scanned file. expected_state_rev is optional.

volumes.declare_tier.note: Recovery after an unknown outcome never resends blindly: same request_id while retained, else read volumes.list and replay only with expected_state_rev (semantics.md section 3).

learning.status.note: Local human-only learning in both dataset classes (personal since q-11); gate is null while learning is open. Candidate scores are relative, not probabilities.

learning.queue.note: The cursor binds catalog_rev and state_rev; a feedback commit makes the next page stale_generation (semantics.md section 5).

collections.update_members.note: expected_state_rev is required. Optional remove_members removes stable member IDs without resolving a live node. Recovery after an unknown outcome: same request_id while retained, else read collections.members and replay only with expected_state_rev (semantics.md section 3).

collections.members.note: The cursor binds catalog_rev and state_rev; a membership change makes the next page stale_generation (semantics.md section 5).

teacher.preview.note: Builds and stores the exact payload. Sends nothing. Personal sessions: capability_unavailable, detail.reason teacher_personal_gated (q-11 opens local learning only; q-5 unmet).

grants.create_disclosure.note: Personal sessions: capability_unavailable, detail.reason teacher_personal_gated (q-11 opens local learning only; q-5 unmet). Beyond that gate, personal dataset: refused with confinement_not_enforced until the docs/41 section 9.2 confinement profile is demonstrated; then native Rust confirmation dialog showing every item (Tauri only). HTTP refuses personal with personal_requires_desktop_dialog. A preview yields at most one grant.

teacher.run.note: The only command that causes network egress, and only via the single-use grant, consumed in state.db before spawn. Launches the pinned native Codex executable under the docs/41 section 9.2 runner profile (ADR-V3-10). Replay with a used grant returns the existing job, never a second disclosure. Personal sessions: capability_unavailable, detail.reason teacher_personal_gated (q-11 opens local learning only; q-5 unmet).

teacher.results.note: Personal sessions: capability_unavailable, detail.reason teacher_personal_gated (q-11 opens local learning only; q-5 unmet).

placement.simulate.note: Synchronous and bounded by node_budget and the deadline; never a job. A request the service estimates it cannot finish in time is deadline_exceeded or resource_budget (retry with a smaller max_groups or node_budget). Default deadline 10,000 ms (semantics.md section 2).

backups.list.note: Imported recovery evidence; ages and staleness are recomputed at read time.

backups.import.note: Rust opens the native open-file dialog (twice with integrity_check), reads at most 256 KiB read-only and stores only normalised evidence. Personal sessions only. HTTP: capability_unavailable. Never runs a backup tool.

backups.forget.note: Removes Loomward's own evidence record; never a backup or a file.

diagnostics.preview.note: A redacted allowlist bundle, its byte count and SHA-256 digest. Keeps the last preview's bytes in memory for diagnostics.save; writes nothing.

diagnostics.save.note: Loomward's first file write (docs/42 ADR-V3-24): Rust opens the native save dialog and writes exactly the previewed bytes whose digest the request names, new file or owner-confirmed replace. The path never crosses IPC. HTTP: capability_unavailable.

stream.hello.rate: first item of every stream, then re-sent as a heartbeat after 15 s without other events on that stream (SSE and Tauri); not sequenced, never replayed (semantics.md section 7)

stream.lagged.rate: when a subscriber queue (1024 events) overflowed; client refetches the named resources

scan.progress.rate: at most 4 per second per job

tree.invalidated.rate: at most 2 per second per root; scope=all at scan finalise

learning.updated.rate: after each feedback commit, refit or teacher result

volumes.changed.rate: volume arrival/removal, tier declaration; polled at most every 10 s

health.warning.rate: deduplicated; at most 1 per code per 30 s
